title: Chauri Chaura
subtitle: The Fire That Stopped a Movement
logline: One town burns a police station, a national movement halts, and the trial hangs nineteen. The case is laid out as evidence: the order, the fire, the argument, and the record.

style.look: ink black, archive paper, thread red, sodium amber, oxidised green; one lamp, paper grain, no reenactment
rules: The room is the world: every scene begins and ends on paper, pins and one lamp.
The red thread is the argument: claim to evidence to consequence, never decoration.
Never show a body or a burning building; the fire is ember, reflection or record.
Every factual card carries the ledger row that proves it, visible on screen.
Camera is a hand over a table, never a drone; no generic stock and no talking heads.

blender.role: procedural sets from the stock archetype library, hero stills

toolchain.encode: ffmpeg H.264/AAC with burned ASS captions

signature: thread test: the red thread from one beat is the rule, route or axis of the next
pin drop: a new fact lands as a pin, not as a lower third
paper seam: the split screen opens like a file, both sides on the same stock
date slide: timelines draw left to right and never jump the thread
room return: every act ends on the table, not on a montage

acts.signature: the mechanism, the return, the coda

scenes.title: THE ANOMALY
scenes.purpose: Cold open on the evidence board. A small district is pinned beside a national halt, and the question is stated before the answer.

narration.text: The Chauri Chaura incident took place on 4 February 1922 in Gorakhpur district.
narration.quote: The Chauri Chaura Incident took place on 4 February 1922 at Chauri Chaura in the Gorakhpur district of United Provinces (now Uttar Pradesh) in British India.

narration.text: Three civilians and 22 policemen died in the incident.
narration.quote: The incident led to the deaths of three civilians and 22 policemen.

narration.text: Gandhi halted the non-cooperation movement on the national level on 12 February 1922.
narration.quote: Mohandas Gandhi halted the non-cooperation movement on the national level on 12 February 1922 as a direct result of the incident.

shots.camera: locked title card, paper grain, a one-percent push
shots.visual: The channel mark lands over ink black: CASE 01 · THE EVIDENCE ROOM, then the case name in two heavy lines.

transition.reason: The thin rule under the title becomes the red thread pinned across the board.

shots.camera: top-down on the board, slow settle
shots.visual: Four paper cards are pinned in a row, joined by one red thread: the date, the dead, the national halt, and a blank WHY card.

transition.reason: The board sheet drags off the table and the district map is already underneath it.

shots.camera: top-down map, one lamp, slow push to the pin
shots.visual: A case map of India under the lamp. The pin lands at Chauri Chaura and a leader line runs to a file card with the date and the crowd.

transition.reason: The pin holds and the count takes the frame.

shots.camera: locked grid, numbers rising with the voice
shots.visual: Four evidence cells: three civilians, 22 policemen, the crowd, and the fifteen local officers. The figures count up once, then hold.

transition.reason: The last number holds and the dates take over.

shots.camera: frontal timeline, thread drawing left to right
shots.visual: A red thread draws a three-point timeline: the incident, the national halt, and Gandhi in prison. Each pin carries its date and ledger tag.

transition.reason: The timeline settles and the room holds on the index wall.

shots.camera: raking side light, slow drift, lens 50
shots.visual: The index wall under one lamp, cards squared, one blank card at the end. The room is quiet enough for the first file.

transition.reason: The wall falls away and the file opens at the beginning.

scenes.title: THE FILE
scenes.purpose: Open the file: the movement, the town, the march, the liquor picket, the arrests. The escalation is a sequence, not a mood.

narration.text: The non-cooperation movement was launched on 4 September 1920 to withdraw cooperation from the British government.
narration.quote: The non-cooperation movement was a political campaign launched on 4 September 1920 by Mahatma Gandhi to encourage Indians to withdraw their cooperation from the British government, with the aim of persuading them to grant self-governance.

narration.text: A protest against the police was called on 4 February, to be held at the bazaar.
narration.quote: In response to this, a protest against the police was called on 4 February, to be held at the Bazaar.

narration.text: Approximately 2,000 to 2,500 protesters assembled and marched towards the market lane.
narration.quote: On 4 February, approximately 2,000 to 2,500 protesters assembled and began marching towards the market lane at Chauri Chaura.

narration.text: A police officer had attacked volunteers picketing a liquor shop.
narration.quote: A police officer had attacked some volunteers picketing a liquor shop.

narration.text: Several of the leaders were arrested and put in the lock-up at the police station.
narration.quote: Several of the leaders were arrested and put in the lock-up at the Chauri Chaura police station.

narration.text: Armed police were dispatched while the protesters marched towards the bazaar, shouting anti-British slogans.
narration.quote: Armed police were dispatched to control the situation while the protesters marched towards the bazaar, shouting anti-British slogans.

shots.camera: frontal timeline, the thread drawing through the dates
shots.visual: The timeline starts in 1920: the movement launched, the first arrests, and the February protest. The thread is the through-line.

transition.reason: The last date holds and the map takes the pin.

shots.camera: top-down map, the pin pressed on the market town
shots.visual: The same map, closer: the case card names the bazaar protest and the crowd that would march into the market lane.

transition.reason: The map sheet lifts and the field is already under the same lamp.

shots.camera: low eye-height wide, dust in the light
shots.visual: Furrows and stubble at dawn, a line of walkers crossing the frame, dust hanging in the low sun.

transition.reason: The march carries across the cut and the picket takes the frame.

shots.camera: macro on a plinth, lens 60, shallow focus
shots.visual: A glass liquor jar on a dark plinth, one amber edge lit, a picket stick leaning beside it.

transition.reason: The jar glass ticks and the lock-up register answers.

shots.camera: slow push along the cards, lens 50
shots.visual: A wall of index cards in six rows, one whole row missing, a clerk stool below and dust in the raking light.

transition.reason: A card slips and the armed police arrive at the gate.

shots.camera: locked wide, eye height, gate centred
shots.visual: The thana gate at dusk, iron bars and one lamp above the arch, armed men arriving in the yard beyond.

transition.reason: The gate holds and the board restates the file.

shots.camera: top-down board, four cards already pinned
shots.visual: Four cards summarise the file so far: the launch, the protest, the arrests, the armed police. The thread runs through all four.

transition.reason: The board clears and the warning shots begin the chain.

scenes.title: THE CHAIN
scenes.purpose: The escalation as a chain of orders and reactions: warning shots, stones, fire, retreat, the burning chowki, and two accounts of why the police fell back.

narration.text: Gupteshwar Singh ordered his 15 local police officers to fire warning shots into the air.
narration.quote: In an attempt to frighten and disperse the crowd, Gupteshwar Singh ordered his 15 local police officers to fire warning shots into the air.

narration.text: The warning shots only agitated the crowd, which began to throw stones at the police.
narration.quote: This only agitated the crowd who began to throw stones at the police.

narration.text: Prithvi Pal ordered the police to open fire on the advancing crowd, killing three.
narration.quote: With the situation getting out of control, the sub-inspector Prithvi Pal ordered the police to open fire on the advancing crowd, killing three and wounding several others.

narration.text: The heavily outnumbered police fell back to the shelter of the town chowki.
narration.quote: In the ensuing chaos, the heavily outnumbered police fell back to the shelter of the town chowki (police station) while the angry mob advanced.

narration.text: The crowd set the chowki ablaze, killing all the policemen trapped inside, including Gupteshwar Singh.
narration.quote: Infuriated by the gunfire into their ranks, the crowd set the chowki a blaze, killing all of the policemen trapped inside, including Inspector Gupteshwar Singh.

narration.text: Reports vary on the police retreat: some constables ran out of ammunition.
narration.quote: Reports vary on the reason for the police retreat, with some suggesting that the constables ran out of ammunition while others claimed that the crowd's unexpectedly assertive reaction to the gunfire was the cause.

narration.text: Others claimed the crowd's unexpectedly assertive reaction to the gunfire caused the retreat.
narration.quote: Reports vary on the reason for the police retreat, with some suggesting that the constables ran out of ammunition while others claimed that the crowd's unexpectedly assertive reaction to the gunfire was the cause.

shots.camera: locked grid, the fifteen counted once
shots.visual: The numbers of the chain: fifteen officers, the crowd, three killed by fire, 22 policemen inside the chowki.

transition.reason: The count lands and the stones start.

shots.camera: low wide, stones in the foreground
shots.visual: Loose stones in the dust, a broken fence rail, the town haze beyond; the ground is the only foreground.

transition.reason: A stone lands and the order to fire takes the frame.

shots.camera: inside the yard, bars in foreground, lens 28
shots.visual: The gate from inside, bars across the foreground, the yard lit by one bulb, the street lost in black.

transition.reason: The bolt draws and the retreat begins.

shots.camera: low angle from the yard, lens 28
shots.visual: The gate from the yard, bars and arch, the lamp above it out and the sky turning to soot.

transition.reason: The gate empties and the embers take the frame.

shots.camera: macro on stone, lens 90, shallow focus
shots.visual: Embers and ash on dark stone, one orange seam breathing; no wall, no roof, no figure in the frame.

transition.reason: Smoke crosses the embers and dissolves into the two accounts of the retreat.

shots.camera: frontal split, the seam opening like a file
shots.visual: The record splits in two: ammunition on the left, the crowd's reaction on the right. Both panels carry the same ledger row.

transition.reason: The seam closes and the aftermath is a wall of names.

shots.camera: slow pull back, lens 50
shots.visual: The index-card wall again, cards browned at the edges, the missing row now a black gap.

transition.reason: A card drops and the corridor of the lock-up opens.

scenes.title: THE SPLIT
scenes.purpose: The political argument: Nehru and Congress workers thought the halt hasty; Gandhi feared a wider slide into violence. The film states both, then follows the arrests.

narration.text: Nehru and most Congress workers, in prison when Gandhi decided, felt the decision was hasty and incorrect.
narration.quote: Jawaharlal Nehru and most of the workers of the Congress, who were in prison when Gandhi made this decision, felt that this was a hasty and incorrect decision at a time when the nation was reaching the epoch of support for the Indian independence movement.

narration.text: The Moplah Rebellion of 1921 had veered away from non-violent methods.
narration.quote: Moplah Rebellion of 1921 had veered away from non-violent methods.

narration.text: In 1921, the Prince of Wales riots saw a Hindu-Muslim mob attack Parsis, Jews and Anglo-Indians.
narration.quote: In 1921, there had been Prince of Wales riots where Parsis, Jews and Anglo-Indians were attacked by a Hindu-Muslim mob which caused large scale destruction.

narration.text: Gandhi did not want the movement to degenerate into a contest of violence.
narration.quote: Mahatma Gandhi did not want the movement to degenerate into a contest of violence, with police and angry mobs attacking each other back and forth, victimizing civilians in between.

narration.text: Although he had stopped the national revolt single-handedly, Gandhi was arrested on 12 February 1922.
narration.quote: Although he had stopped the national revolt single-handedly, on 12 February 1922, Mahatma Gandhi was arrested.

narration.text: On 18 March 1922, he was imprisoned for six years for publishing seditious materials.
narration.quote: On 18 March 1922, he was imprisoned for six years for publishing seditious materials.

narration.text: This led to the suppression of the movement and the arrest of other leaders.
narration.quote: This led to the suppression of the movement and was followed by the arrest of other leaders.

shots.camera: wide from the window, lens 35
shots.visual: A meeting room with empty chairs, a table and a half-drawn blind; one paper sits where a speaker would stand.

transition.reason: The empty chair holds and the 1921 file opens.

shots.camera: frontal, raking light, lens 50
shots.visual: A wall of newspaper pages pasted edge to edge, headlines turned away, the paste dark and the paper cockled.

transition.reason: A page flaps and the second 1921 file takes the frame.

shots.camera: low wide, smoke in the middle distance, lens 30
shots.visual: A field at dusk with stubble smoke standing in still air, a fence and one tree, no figures in the frame.

transition.reason: The smoke bends and the argument is laid out in two panels.

shots.camera: frontal split, both panels on the same paper stock
shots.visual: The split is the argument: on the left the dissent that the halt was hasty, on the right Gandhi's fear of a contest of violence.

graphic.note: Both claims sit in the same record.

transition.reason: The seam closes and the arrest follows.

shots.camera: exterior, rain on bars, lens 45
shots.visual: A jail gate in rain, the lamp halo soft, a warder's shadow just outside the frame and the street empty.

transition.reason: Rain on the bars carries the cut into the cell.

shots.camera: inside the cell, lens 45
shots.visual: A cell door ajar, the stone floor catching a wedge of corridor light, the cot stripped to the frame.

transition.reason: The hinge turns and the corridor repeats.

shots.camera: from the far end, doors repeating, lens 30
shots.visual: The corridor from its far end, doors repeating, one open and the rest closed, the floor wet with light.

transition.reason: A far door closes and the trial ledger opens.

scenes.title: THE MECHANISM
scenes.purpose: The machinery of the case: raids, custody, the eight-month trial, the High Court appeal, nineteen death sentences, fourteen life sentences, and the hangings.

narration.text: Several raids were conducted and hundreds of people were arrested.
narration.quote: Several raids were conducted and hundreds of people were arrested.

narration.text: Six of the accused died while in police custody.
narration.quote: Of these, six died while in police custody, two were sentenced to two years' imprisonment, 170 were convicted and sentenced to death by hanging while 47 were acquitted on 9 January 1923, following a trial which lasted eight months.

narration.text: 170 were convicted and 47 were acquitted after an eight-month trial.
narration.quote: Of these, six died while in police custody, two were sentenced to two years' imprisonment, 170 were convicted and sentenced to death by hanging while 47 were acquitted on 9 January 1923, following a trial which lasted eight months.

narration.text: Two of the accused were sentenced to two years' imprisonment.
narration.quote: Of these, six died while in police custody, two were sentenced to two years' imprisonment, 170 were convicted and sentenced to death by hanging while 47 were acquitted on 9 January 1923, following a trial which lasted eight months.

narration.text: On 30 April 1923, the High Court of Allahabad pronounced the final judgements.
narration.quote: On 30 April 1923, the High Court of Allahabad pronounced the final judgements in the case, after appeals had been considered regarding the 170 convicted accused, who had been awarded death sentences: The (19) people who were sentenced to death were - 1.

narration.text: Nineteen demonstrators received death sentences and 14 received life imprisonment.
narration.quote: Nineteen arrested demonstrators were sentenced to death and 14 to life imprisonment by the British colonial authorities. == Background == From 1920 onwards, Indians, led by Mohandas Gandhi, were engaged in a nationwide non-cooperation movement.

narration.text: The court reviewed the appeals of the 170 convicted accused.
narration.quote: On 30 April 1923, the High Court of Allahabad pronounced the final judgements in the case, after appeals had been considered regarding the 170 convicted accused, who had been awarded death sentences: The (19) people who were sentenced to death were - 1.

narration.text: The 19 condemned to death were hanged between 2 and 11 July 1923.
narration.quote: The 19 defendants condemned to death were hanged between 2 and 11 July 1923. == Memorial == A memorial to the dead policemen was dedicated by the British colonial authorities in 1923.

shots.camera: steady lateral move, lens 35
shots.visual: A jail corridor with doors on both sides, a bucket and a folded blanket on the floor, one bulb at the far end.

transition.reason: The corridor ends at the cell door.

shots.camera: from the corridor, bars in foreground, lens 34
shots.visual: A cell seen through bars: a cot, a bucket, a high slit window and one blade of cold light on the wall.

transition.reason: The bar taps and the trial count takes the frame.

shots.camera: locked grid, the four trial figures counting up
shots.visual: The trial ledger in four cells: 170 convicted, 47 acquitted, eight months, six dead in custody.

transition.reason: The last cell holds and the two-year sentence takes the desk.

shots.camera: overhead, ribbon marker in focus, lens 46
shots.visual: The trial ledger open at a page of names, a red ribbon marker at the fold and the desk lamp low.

transition.reason: The ribbon pulls free and the High Court page appears.

shots.camera: high desk, seal in foreground, lens 50
shots.visual: A high court desk with a judgement sheet, a wax seal, a glass of water and everything else in black.

transition.reason: The seal presses and the sentence count takes over.

shots.camera: locked grid, the appeal figures held
shots.visual: Four appeal figures: nineteen death sentences, fourteen life sentences, 170 appeals, and the date of the final judgement.

transition.reason: The date holds and the appeal page returns.

shots.camera: frontal, sheets aligned, lens 50
shots.visual: The notice wall with every sheet aligned, the missing gap filled by one blank page, the light hard from the left.

transition.reason: The blank sheet settles and the jail gate takes the last line.

shots.camera: first light, wet bars, lens 40
shots.visual: The jail gate at first light, the bars wet and the street empty; the date of the hangings is the only text in the frame.

transition.reason: The gate holds and the film returns to the lake.

scenes.title: THE RETURN
scenes.purpose: Return to paper and memory: the 1971 association, the 1973 minaret, the subscription, the colonial police memorial, and Nehru's word for the end.

narration.text: In 1971, local inhabitants formed an association named Chauri Chaura Shaheed Smarak Samiti.
narration.quote: In 1971, local inhabitants formed an association named Chauri Chaura Shaheed Smarak Samiti.

narration.text: In 1973, this Samiti constructed near the lake a 12.2-metre-tall triangular minaret.
narration.quote: In 1973, this Samiti constructed near the lake at Chauri Chaura a 12.2-metre-tall (40 ft) triangular minaret on each side of which a figure is depicted hanging with a noose around his neck.

narration.text: Each side of the minaret depicts a figure hanging with a noose around his neck.
narration.quote: In 1973, this Samiti constructed near the lake at Chauri Chaura a 12.2-metre-tall (40 ft) triangular minaret on each side of which a figure is depicted hanging with a noose around his neck.

narration.text: The minaret was built at a cost of Rs 13,500 contributed by popular subscription.
narration.quote: The minaret was built at a cost of Rs 13,500 contributed by popular subscription.

narration.text: A memorial to the dead policemen was dedicated by the British colonial authorities in 1923.
narration.quote: The 19 defendants condemned to death were hanged between 2 and 11 July 1923. == Memorial == A memorial to the dead policemen was dedicated by the British colonial authorities in 1923.

narration.text: Nehru described the movement as ending suddenly on 4 February 1922.
narration.quote: The non-cooperation movement was among the broader movement for Indian independence from British rule and ended, as Nehru described in his autobiography, "suddenly" on 4 February 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.

shots.camera: wide at dusk, steps leading to water, lens 38
shots.visual: Stone steps down to a wide river, one boat and a hanging lamp; the far bank is a dark line.

transition.reason: Water laps and the memorial photograph takes the frame.

shots.camera: document insert, slow push across the print
shots.visual: A modern photograph of the Chauri Chaura memorial, pinned beside the case note: a triangular minaret above the lake.

transition.reason: The print lifts and the flame holds the next line.

shots.camera: macro, flame centred, lens 85
shots.visual: A small flame in a glass on a dark table, the only warm thing in the room, its halo on the glass.

transition.reason: The flame breathes and the subscription figures appear.

shots.camera: locked grid, the cost and the date held together
shots.visual: Four figures from the memorial file: the subscription, the year, the height, and the association that built it.

transition.reason: The figures hold and the colonial memorial returns.

shots.camera: frontal, raking light, lens 50
shots.visual: The notice wall with one sheet squared at eye height, the rest turned away; the colonial memorial is a document, not a monument.

transition.reason: The sheet settles and the case returns to four cards.

shots.camera: top-down board, the four cards already joined
shots.visual: The case in four cards: the incident, the halt, the hangings, and the minaret. The red thread ties the dates together.

transition.reason: The red thread pulls taut and becomes the rule under the closing title.

scenes.title: CODA
scenes.purpose: Close on the channel mark and the promise that governs every case file.

shots.camera: locked title card, the room dimming to black
shots.visual: The closing card: the case name, the channel mark, and the line that governs the archive.

transition.reason: The lamp goes down and the room closes to black.
